title: Banco Central Holds Benchmark Rate at 4.5% — Third Consecutive Hold
detail: Chile's Central Bank held its benchmark policy rate at 4.50% for the third consecutive monetary policy meeting on April 28, 2026 — the lowest level since Q1 2022. The decision reflected the Board's assessment that inflationary pressure from March's dramatic fuel price increases (gasoline up 32%, diesel up 62%) had not yet filtered fully into expectations, while tightening further risked over-correction. Analysts polled by Bloomberg had expected a hold; the decision underscored the difficult balancing act facing the new Kast administration, which inherited both a fragile economy and a politically charged fuel pricing environment that had already triggered cacerolazos (pot-banging protests) in March and April.

media.caption: Chile's Central Bank holds policy rate at 4.5% for third straight meeting amid fuel-driven inflation pressures

title: Kast Approval Slides to 29.1% — Lowest of His Term — As Fuel Protests Persist
detail: Pulso Ciudadano polling released in late April 2026 showed President José Antonio Kast's approval rating at 29.1%, the lowest point since his inauguration on March 11, 2026, with disapproval rising to 55.6%. Only 24.1% approved of ministerial performance against 62.7% disapproval. The collapse — from 59% approval at inauguration — followed fuel price increases of 32% for gasoline and 62% for diesel announced on March 23, triggering the largest protests Chile had seen since the 2019 estallido social. The government introduced transport subsidies and frozen transit fares as palliative measures, but the political damage had already registered with a public that was already stretched thin by post-pandemic cost-of-living pressures.

media.caption: Kast's approval falls to 29.1% — lowest since inauguration — as fuel price protests persist
